n: NFT and Online Gaming / In-Game Currency Laundering
ds: Non-fungible tokens and in-game currencies can be bought, sold or transferred with subjective or opaque values, enabling wash trading, self-dealing and conversion of illicit funds into items that are later resold. Gaming platforms also host cross-border micro-transfers that hide value movement.

src.t: US Department of the Treasury, Illicit Finance Risk Assessment of Non-Fungible Tokens (2024)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
FATF, Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing in the Art and Antiquities Market (2023)

rat: NFT marketplaces and game economies; wash trading between wallets, in-game currency cash-out and stolen-card funding.

ind.n: Wash trading between wallets controlled by the same party
ind.cx: NFTs are sold repeatedly between linked wallets at rising prices without genuine third-party demand.
ind.fp: Collectors moving assets between own wallets.
ind.ds: Assets or securities are traded repeatedly between linked accounts or wallets at unrealistic prices.
ind.cn: Wash or matched trades between connected parties

ind.n: Purchase price far above comparable floor or last sale
ind.cx: A buyer pays a large premium for an item without supporting valuation.
ind.ds: Price paid differs sharply from market value, comparable sales or estimates without commercial justification.
ind.cn: Transaction price materially different from market value

ind.n: Newly minted NFT sold immediately for large sums to unrelated wallet
ind.cx: Creator mints and sells quickly to a single buyer funded by a cluster with no history.
ind.ds: Creator mints and sells quickly to a single buyer funded by a cluster with no history.

ind.n: Fast conversion of in-game currency to cash or crypto
ind.cx: Large currency amounts earned or received are cashed out through third-party sites within a short period.
ind.ds: Large currency amounts earned or received are cashed out through third-party sites within a short period.

ind.n: Many low-value in-game transfers from unrelated accounts to one account
ind.cx: Fan-in of small gifts or trades into a single collector, then withdrawal.
ind.ds: Numerous unrelated payers send frequent, often small, payments to one account, wallet or beneficiary, or one funder pays many beneficiaries, with no clear commercial relationship.
ind.cn: Many unrelated senders paying a single account or recipient

ind.n: Accounts bought with stolen cards then items resold
ind.cx: Chargebacks on purchases of currency or items followed by transfer to other accounts.
ind.ds: Chargebacks on purchases of currency or items followed by transfer to other accounts.

ind.n: Marketplace sellers with no identity verification receiving large payouts
ind.cx: Pseudonymous sellers withdraw significant proceeds to fiat or exchange wallets.
ind.ds: Pseudonymous sellers withdraw significant proceeds to fiat or exchange wallets.

ind.n: Use of mixers or privacy tools before purchasing NFTs
ind.cx: Purchase funding traces through obfuscation services.
ind.ds: Funds pass through mixers, privacy coins or privacy-preserving pools before or after platform activity without commercial rationale.
ind.cn: Use of mixers, privacy coins or privacy pools around platform activity

ind.n: Sanctioned or high-risk jurisdiction counterparties in game economies
ind.cx: Transfers or sales involve users in sanctioned regions, detected via geolocation or wallet data.
ind.ds: Funds, counterparties or institutions are located in jurisdictions with weak AML supervision, sanctions exposure or limited VASP regulation.
ind.cn: Counterparty or flows in higher-risk jurisdictions with weak AML controls

ind.n: Marketplace or game operator lacks AML controls
ind.cx: Operator permits unlimited withdrawal and trade, ignores abuse reports and does not verify high-value users.
ind.ds: Operator permits unlimited withdrawal and trade, ignores abuse reports and does not verify high-value users.

ctl.ds: Traces exposure of deposit and withdrawal addresses to illicit clusters and screens wallets with risk-scored alerts. It reveals on-chain exposure.
Links accounts, devices, addresses, directors and beneficiaries to surface rings, shared attributes and flow structures that single-account views miss. It supports detection of organised networks.

ctl.n: Specialist investigation and suspicious activity reporting
ctl.ds: Trained analysts investigate alerts with typology playbooks, document rationale and file reports where suspicion is formed, with prompt reporting to the competent authority. It converts alerts into actionable intelligence.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.

Caps transaction size, frequency, load, withdrawal and deposit values, with staged increases as legitimate behaviour is established and per-customer limits at kiosks. It bounds the loss and laundering capacity of new or higher-risk accounts.

Monitors merchant-level patterns such as ticket size, refund, void and chargeback rates, descriptor mismatch and cross-merchant flows. It identifies transaction laundering, bust-out and illicit merchants.

Applies additional information gathering, corroboration, monitoring and senior review to relationships or transactions assessed as higher risk, covering purpose, expected activity, ownership and funds. The depth is proportionate to the risk drivers identified.

ctl.n: Seller, organiser and payee verification with payout controls
ctl.ds: Verifies sellers, workers and fundraising organisers, matches payees to verified identities and holds or staggers payouts for new or anomalous accounts. It limits platform abuse.

Obtains and tests documentary evidence of where the money for a transaction, deposit or capital injection comes from, particularly when value exceeds thresholds or the customer profile. It reduces the chance that illicit proceeds are accepted without explanation.

Screens customers, owners, counterparties, vessels, dealers and addresses against sanctions, enforcement and restricted-party lists at onboarding and ongoing, using fuzzy matching and secondary identifiers. Potential matches are held for adjudication before service or funds are released.

ctl.n: Funds hold, freeze and recall procedure
ctl.ds: Provides a defined, legally grounded capability to restrict, hold, freeze or recall funds and accounts pending review or on confirmed exposure, with clear triggers and approvers. It stops onward dissipation of suspected illicit funds.

Detects use of VPN, proxy and anonymising services and compares access geolocation with declared residence and sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions. It reveals concealed location and supports geographic restrictions.

Matches accounts, devices, identifiers and beneficiaries against industry fraud sharing and ingests law-enforcement, commercial and open-source threat feeds, including victim reports from other institutions. It catches known bad actors early.

ctl.n: Risk appetite and product policy statements
ctl.ds: Documents the institution's appetite and permitted or prohibited products, assets and activities for a given risk area, with limits and review cadence. It gives staff and systems a clear boundary for acceptance.
